task.description: Idiom/OTP/scope-creep review (hard gate) on REQ-062's implementation, branch feature/WF02-REQ062-20260819 already checked out. SECURITY-REVIEWER already PASSed (step-02c). Note two things ELIXIR-DEV self-flagged as honest scope limitations (not silent gaps): (1) OQ-3 nested/grandchild SUB_PROCESS activation not recursively wired -- check whether this is an acceptable scope boundary for THIS requirement's 8 ACs or should have blocked; (2) a PARALLEL_GATEWAY split/join branch landing directly on a SUB_PROCESS node within the same hop chain is rejected with a typed error rather than handled, mirroring a pre-existing similar limitation elsewhere in the same function. Also note ELIXIR-DEV made one cross-cutting decision worth scrutiny: widening Engine.advance_until_stable/4's return from a 2-tuple to a 3-tuple and adapting REQ-053's reconstruction.ex call sites to match (a genuine regression it found and fixed within this same run, not gold-plating) -- confirm this was the right call vs. e.g. a separate function.
acceptance_criteria: Idiomatic OTP vs. crutch check per .claude/agents/reviewer.md's four questions

Supervision integrity check -- does this touch process_instance.ex/instance_supervisor.ex, and if not, was the design's claim that S3 runs instances as plain Ecto.Multi code (no supervision change needed) verified true
Scope creep check -- is everything touched actually load-bearing for REQ-062, including the reconstruction.ex regression fix and the advance_until_stable/4 signature widening
Consistency with docs/migration/decisions/ -- nothing in this diff should silently contradict a decision record

docs/anti-patterns.md checked for any recurring mistake class this diff might repeat (migration version-prefix collision, describe/test name length -- N/A here since no tests yet, git rebase --ours/--theirs -- N/A, module-name collision)

result.summary:
AC1 (idiom/OTP four-question check): PASS. No gen_statem/GenServer involved at this stage -- S3 correctly runs instance transitions as pure Ecto.Multi-composed functions, matching every sibling module (TaskActivation, ExecutionError). SubProcess module performs zero spawn/Process work; its only pre-Multi Repo reads (prepare_child_activation/4, append_completion_multi/6) are documented, justified exceptions (must-write-nothing-on-failure), reentrant against the caller's own already-open transaction, same shape TaskActivation/create_snapshot already establish -- not a crutch. Transition.ex's new :SUB_PROCESS dispatch clauses (dispatch_sub_process_entry/4, dispatch_sub_process_completion/4) stay pure (zero I/O, zero child creation), correctly deferring all writes to the Engine/SubProcess layer -- the purity contract is upheld, not worked around. advance_off_completed_node/4 extraction (shared between HUMAN_TASK and SUB_PROCESS completion) is a genuine, non-duplicative reuse, not premature abstraction.
AC2 (supervision integrity): PASS. `git diff --stat` confirms process_instance.ex/instance_supervisor.ex are untouched by this diff. Verified directly: Engine.create/2's own root-instance insert_instance_projection/8 never sets parent_instance_id/parent_token_id (lib/letflow/engine.ex:757-774), and SubProcess.insert_child_instance_projection/8 is the only call site that does -- confirming the design's 'plain Ecto.Multi code, no supervision change needed' claim is actually true in the diff, not just asserted in the design doc.
AC3 (scope creep): PASS, with the advance_until_stable/4 widening and reconstruction.ex adaptation judged the correct call, not gold-plating. The widening is the minimum non-additive change needed to let a pure activation loop report 'a child needs creating' back to an I/O-capable caller (3 call sites -- activate/3, dispatch_task_completion_hop_chain/5, Reconstruction.replay -- all updated consistently, all but the new SUB_PROCESS consumer unaffected in behavior). A separate function would have duplicated the entire recursive hop-walking logic across two versions that must stay in lockstep -- strictly worse. Reconstruction.ex's drop_pending_events/1 adapter cleanly re-restores that module's own pre-existing 2-tuple contract rather than threading pending-event lists through unrelated replay code, and its new SUB_PROCESS_COMPLETED replay clause is load-bearing (REQ-062 durably persists this event type; a reconstruction path that couldn't replay it would silently desync). No abstraction (behaviour, macro, generic plumbing) introduced ahead of what REQ-062's 8 ACs need.
OQ-3 (nested/grandchild SUB_PROCESS not recursively wired): checked directly against REQ-062's 8 acceptance_criteria in docs/requirements.yaml -- none mention nested/grandchild sub-processes or cross-definition recursion depth. Acceptable scope boundary for this requirement, correctly named (not silently dropped) in both the design doc §9 OQ-3 and the module's own moduledoc.
Split/join-on-SUB_PROCESS rejection (cast_parent_token_record_id/1, engine.ex): confirmed as a typed error path ({:sub_process_after_split_join_not_supported, token_id}), not silently swallowed or a raise, and confirmed to mirror the pre-existing do_reconcile_token_records/4 {:new_token_during_resume_not_supported, ...} limitation by the same mechanism (derived vs. persisted token_id). No REQ-062 AC exercises this path. Correct call for this run's scope -- filed as ISS-0067 (see issues below) because the mechanism both sites now share (UUID-castability as a proxy for 'is this token_id persisted') is a runtime heuristic standing in for a type distinction, which is exactly this role's type-safety-gap criterion, even though it isn't new to this diff.
AC4 (decision-record consistency): PASS. Migration correctly follows decision 0006/REQ-022 §4's tenant-scoped-migration convention (`if prefix() do` guard wraps both the alter table and both new indexes, verified by reading the file). instance_projections is one of D2's eight schema-isolated business tables (no tenant_id column) -- the new parent_instance_id/parent_token_id columns are plain scalar FKs on an already-schema-isolated table, correctly not reintroducing a tenant_id-shaped column. Matches SECURITY-REVIEWER's own step-02c INV-1 finding (prefix threaded consistently, no second/independent prefix introduced).
AC5 (anti-patterns.md / migration + module collision check): PASS. New migration timestamp 20260819045553 sits between 20260819000005 and 20260820000001 in priv/repo/migrations/ with no collision (`ls | sort` confirms uniqueness). `grep -rl "defmodule Letflow.Engine.SubProcess"` returns exactly one file (lib/letflow/engine/sub_process.ex) -- no module-name collision. No other anti-patterns.md entry class (timestamp extrapolation, docker-compose worktree misuse, requirement_status.yaml overwrite, task-selection fallback) applies to this diff.
issues: ISS-0067 (MINOR, type-safety, filed this step, github.com/tvolodi/letflow/issues/228): the 'is this token_id a real persisted TokenRecord id, or a derived split/join branch id never given its own row' distinction is decided at runtime by UUID-castability (engine.ex's new cast_parent_token_record_id/1) or set-membership (the pre-existing do_reconcile_token_records/4) rather than by any type. This diff adds a second site relying on the same heuristic rather than introducing a type-level tag -- not blocking (no REQ-062 AC exercises the path), but worth a future requirement fixing the root cause once, not per-site.

OQ-1 (SUB_PROCESS node's definition_name attribute) remains an explicitly-flagged, unverified assumption per the design doc and module moduledoc -- not verified against R-Co source in this environment, correctly surfaced rather than silently built against. Not blocking; flagged for whoever next has R-Co source access to confirm.

OQ-4 (a child cancelled directly leaves the parent's token permanently :waiting, no cascade notification) is a known, honestly-named gap with no owning requirement yet -- not a REQ-062 AC, correctly not addressed here, worth tracking when EE-08's reverse direction gets its own requirement.
